before: picture lets a browser choose an image source based on conditions while one img supplies the displayed image and alt text.
A source uses srcset for candidates. A media condition can select a different crop. ```html ```
The browser considers source elements in order and uses a suitable match. The img remains necessary as the fallback and the image element itself.
min-width includes its boundary. This example selects its wide candidate at 800px as well as wider viewports.
Changing the crop to suit the composition is called art direction. It differs from offering several resolutions of the same image.
Place alt on img, not source. The description should remain appropriate for every crop.
The exercise filenames are placeholders. Markup checks cannot prove that the files exist, that the crop is useful, or which resource a real browser downloads.
after: `` lets the browser choose an image source that fits a condition. A source can offer a wider crop for a wider screen. The `` inside still provides the image element and its text description.

This example offers a wide lake picture on wider screens. ```html ``` `media` gives the width condition. `srcset` names the wide picture. The img’s `src` supplies the fallback picture when no source matches. Its `alt` describes the scene.
Put source elements before img. The browser considers the sources in order and uses a suitable match. Keep img even when you have a source; it is still needed.
`min-width: 800px` means 800 pixels wide or wider. The exact boundary counts. Here, the width is the browser’s page-viewing area.
A crop shows a chosen part of a picture. Choosing different crops for different layouts is called art direction. Offering sharper versions of the same crop is a separate idea.
Put `alt` on img, not source. It should describe the useful information shared by all the crops. If a crop removes that information, rethink the crop or its description.

after.question: A source uses min-width: 600px. Does it match at exactly 600px?
choices: Yes. The minimum width is included.
Only if img uses the same filename.
after.explanation: A minimum includes its stated boundary, so 600px matches.
